plan.analysis: Baseline is the constant function (R=2/3). A Gaussian profile is known to give R=1/sqrt(2)≈0.7071, so the first real gain should come from a smooth bell shape plus local refinement. The open question is whether shapes flatter or sharper than a Gaussian (e.g. generalized Gaussian exp(-|x|^p), or a smoothed box) push the autoconvolution closer to a plateau and beat 0.7071. I will spend the deepen slot on Gaussian + hill-climbing, and the two explore slots on parametric families that interpolate between box and Gaussian, each with its own local search, so the next generation can branch from whichever family wins.

experiments.hypothesis: A discretized Gaussian has R≈0.7071, well above the constant's 2/3; local multiplicative hill-climbing on the heights will polish it further.
experiments.change: Ignore start's shape. Set N=200, x=arange(N)-(N-1)/2. Try s in {15,20,25,30}: h=exp(-0.5*(x/s)**2), compute R with the exact formula (L=[0,*np.convolve(h,h),0]; R=sum(L_j^2+L_j L_{j+1}+L_{j+1}^2)/3 / ((sum h)^2 * max(L))), keep the best. Then, while time.process_time()<0.9*budget: pick random index i, multiply h[i] by exp(uniform(-0.05,0.05)), recompute R, accept if R increased; every 2000 iterations also try one larger step exp(uniform(-0.3,0.3)). Return best h.
experiments.prediction: R rises to about 0.700-0.712, clearly above 0.666667.
experiments.if_gain: Next deepen: increase N to 400, add simulated-annealing acceptance and coordinate sweeps; also test whether the refined profile's tails/shoulders are systematically shaped (record the best h for branching).
experiments.if_not: If no gain, the R computation or N is wrong; verify with a pure Gaussian of known R, then retry with N=100 and s=10.

experiments.hypothesis: The generalized Gaussian family f=exp(-|x|^p) interpolates between Laplace (p=1), Gaussian (p=2) and box-like (p large); scanning p measures whether p≠2 beats the Gaussian's 0.7071.
experiments.change: From scratch (ignore start). N=300, x=(arange(N)-(N-1)/2)/(N/6) so support ≈±3. For p in 1.0,1.2,1.4,...,3.0: h=exp(-abs(x)**p), compute R, keep best (p*,h*). Then run the same multiplicative hill-climb as slot 1 on h* until 0.9*budget, and also try small changes to the scale (x/(N/6) replaced by x/(c*N/6), c in {0.7,1.0,1.4}). Return best h.
experiments.prediction: Best p is near 2.0 with R≈0.707; if p* is clearly below or above 2, that is a strong signal to follow.
experiments.if_gain: If p*≠2 gives R>0.71, branch on that p with finer p grid and larger N. If p*≈2, treat Gaussian as the current best family and focus branching on the smoothed-box family.
experiments.if_not: If all p give R<0.70, the discretization is too coarse; increase N and re-scan, else conclude the family is not promising and rely on slot 3.

experiments.if_gain: If a>0 wins, branch with finer (a,w) grid, larger N, and try box convolved with a generalized-Gaussian kernel; also inspect whether the optimal f*f has a visible plateau.

plan.analysis: p0004 (0.8328) is the clear best: N=50, 24% zeros, and — importantly — its f*f peaks at 0.390 of the support, so the winning f is asymmetric, unlike every smooth symmetric seed tried (all stuck at 0.79-0.80). The jump came in the restart stage, not the refine stage, so the local search/perturbation scheme is doing the work at coarse N. Two deepen bets: (a) p0004's shape is only partly optimized — block/segment moves plus full coordinate sweeps should push it; (b) it may be a coarse-grid optimum, so upsampling + re-polish tests whether finer structure helps. The branch tests F5 directly: give the Gaussian line p0004's search machinery at N=50 — if it reaches ~0.83, the search (not the seed) is the driver.

experiments.hypothesis: p0004's 0.8328 came from single-index perturbations; the asymmetric, partly-zero optimum is under-optimized, and block/segment moves with full coordinate sweeps will find a better local optimum at the same N=50.
experiments.change: Keep p0004's score(). Start h = start (50 heights). Stage 1: coordinate ascent — repeat sweeps over all indices, at each index trying d in (+s,-s,+s/2,-s/2) with s = 0.2*mean, and halve s when a full sweep gives no improvement; stop at s<1e-4*mean. Stage 2 until 0.97*budget: copy best, pick random i and length k in 1..max(2,N//4), add a random smooth perturbation to h[i:i+k] (either constant delta*U(-1,1) or a linear ramp delta*(2*t/k-1), delta ~ 0.15*mean), clip at 0, then run up to 300 single-index coordinate steps (step 0.02*mean) on that copy; accept only if score > best. Print best every ~2 s. Return best.
experiments.prediction: Score rises above 0.8328, to about 0.84-0.86, with the f*f peak staying off-centre and zeros persisting or growing.
experiments.if_gain: Next deepen: freeze the found shape, run a longer block-move search with annealing acceptance and finer block lengths; also record which indices are zero to see if the support is a fixed compact interval.
experiments.if_not: If block moves do not beat 0.8328, the coarse single-index restart scheme is already near a local optimum at N=50; then pivot the deepens to resolution changes and to explicitly asymmetric parametric seeds.

experiments.hypothesis: The N=50 optimum may be a coarse-grid version of a smoother asymmetric shape; upsampling p0004's heights and re-polishing at N=100/200 will either beat 0.8328 (finer structure helps) or show that coarse N is essential.
experiments.change: Keep p0004's score(). From start (N=50), build candidates at N=50, 100, 200 by linear interpolation (np.interp of heights onto the finer grid, i.e. piecewise-linear upsampling). For each N in [50,100,200] give it ~1/3 of the budget: run coordinate ascent (step ladder 0.1,0.05,0.02,0.01*mean) then perturbed restarts exactly as p0004 (perturb ~N//20 random entries with 0.05*mean noise, then 300 refine iterations), always keeping the global best across all N and printing 'N=.. -> score' at each stage end. Also seed N=100 and N=200 from the cosine bump as a control. Return the global best (any N).
experiments.prediction: Upsampled N=100/200 versions score within ~0.005 of 0.8328 or slightly above; if they clearly lose (>0.01 below), the coarse grid is essential to the optimum.
experiments.if_gain: If a finer N wins, next deepen stays at that N and adds block moves; if the gain is tiny, treat N=50 as the right resolution and spend the next deepen on shape families instead.
experiments.if_not: If finer N is worse, keep N=50 as the working resolution and use the next deepen to test explicit asymmetric parametric seeds (one-sided exponential decay, ramp times bump) at N=50.

experiments.hypothesis: F5 is unresolved: p0004's edge may come from its search (coordinate ascent + perturbed restarts) rather than its cosine seed. Applying that exact search to the Gaussian line at N=50 will separate the two.
experiments.change: Take start (p0005's 200 heights), block-average it down to N=50 (np.add.reduceat over 4-blocks, or np.interp onto 50 points), then run p0004's search verbatim: coordinate ascent with step ladder down to 1e-4*mean, then until 0.97*budget repeatedly perturb ~N//20 random entries with 0.05*mean Gaussian noise, refine 300 iterations, keep best. Print stage scores. Return best.
experiments.prediction: If the search is the driver, this reaches ~0.82-0.83 (close to p0004) despite the Gaussian seed; if the seed/shape is the driver it stalls at 0.79-0.80.
experiments.if_gain: If it reaches ~0.83, the search scheme is the key asset: next branch applies p0004's search to the p0007 generalized-Gaussian line, and deepens focus on search improvements rather than seeds.
experiments.if_not: If it stalls near 0.80, the compact asymmetric cosine-seeded shape is special; next branch instead seeds asymmetric one-sided shapes and reruns the same search.

plan.analysis: p0012's +0.00095 shows finer N helps a little, but the N=50 basin is exhausted (p0010: +0.000001). Gains are now tiny, so the bottleneck is local-search precision and basin choice. Bet: (1) an exact analytic gradient of R makes local ascent far sharper than coordinate moves, so p0012's basin can be pushed further and at N=200; (2) large structured perturbations with a fast gradient inner loop can escape that basin; (3) a sparse few-box construction reaches shapes free-form height search cannot, opening a new line. All three are cheap to evaluate exactly, and each has a clear fallback if it fails.

experiments.hypothesis: Coordinate ascent on 100 heights converges slowly and imprecisely; the exact gradient of R (E/(S^2*M)) with a projected-gradient/Armijo scheme will reach a sharper local maximum of the same basin and, continued at N=200, add real gain.
experiments.change: Keep score(). Add grad(h) returning (R, dR/dh) with: L=convolve(h,h); Lp=[0,L,0]; E=(1/3)sum(Lp_j^2+Lp_j Lp_{j+1}+Lp_{j+1}^2); g_j=dE/dLp_j=(1/3)(2Lp_j+Lp_{j-1}+Lp_{j+1}); G_k=g_{k+1}; dE/dh_i=2*sum_k G_k*h_{k-i} (implement with np.convolve(G,h[::-1]) and slice; VERIFY against central finite differences on 5 random indices, print max rel error, and if >1e-4 fall back to the existing coord_ascent). dM/dh_i=2*h_{k*-i} with k*=argmax(L) (average over ties). dS/dh=1. dR = dE/(S^2*M) - 2E/(S^3*M) - E*dM/(S^2*M^2). Stage A (0-40% budget): h=start (N=100); projected gradient ascent h<-max(0,h+t*d), d=grad scaled so max|d|=mean(h), t by backtracking from 0.5, halving until R improves, stop after 5 non-improving steps. Stage B (40-95%): upsample best to N=200 via np.interp on cell centers, repeat projected gradient. Stage C: coordinate ascent (steps 0.02,0.01,0.005,0.002*mean) on the global best. Print score after each stage.
experiments.prediction: Score rises to 0.835-0.838 (gain 0.001-0.004), with the f*f plateau fraction (knots within 1% of max) increasing above 26%.
experiments.if_gain: Next deepen: run the same gradient scheme at N=400 from the N=200 result and check whether plateau fraction and R keep rising with N; if yes, treat N as a free knob and push it.
experiments.if_not: If gradient ascent returns essentially p0012's score, the basin is the binding limit, not the optimizer: next deepen relies on basin hopping (slot 2) and on structural families; also check the finite-difference verification line to confirm the gradient was right.

experiments.hypothesis: p0012 sits in one local basin found by coordinate moves; large structured perturbations followed by a fast gradient inner loop can reach a different, better basin at similar N, which the tiny coordinate perturbations of p0010 could not.
experiments.change: Reuse score() and the verified grad() from the plan above (same finite-difference check; fall back to coordinate polish if it fails). Set N=100, h*=start, R*=score, run 100 projected-gradient steps to polish. Then loop until 95% of budget: copy h*, apply ONE random move: (a) multiply a random contiguous segment of length U(5,30) by U(0.5,2.0); (b) add a Gaussian bump with random center, width U(3,20) cells, amplitude 0.25*mean; (c) zero a random contiguous segment of length U(2,10); (d) replace a random segment by its reverse. Then run 150 projected-gradient steps (same Armijo rule, t starting at 0.3) and accept if R>R*. Every 5th outer iteration instead restart from a fresh cos^2 bump at N=100, gradient-polish 100 steps, and accept if better (diversification). Print best every 2 s. At the end upsample the best to N=200, gradient-polish until near the deadline, then coordinate-ascent polish (steps 0.01,0.005,0.002*mean). Return the global best.
experiments.prediction: Either a gain of 0.001-0.003 (a better basin exists) or no real change, which would confirm p0012's basin is robust and shift effort to structure and N.
experiments.if_gain: Next deepen: take the new basin, map its structure (zero positions, asymmetry, peak location) and run the same hopping at N=200; also seed a branch from it.
experiments.if_not: If hopping never beats p0012, the coarse-N asymmetric shape is a strong attractor: next deepen tests whether the symmetric subspace (average h with its reverse, re-polish) reaches the same score, which would tell us asymmetry is not causal and let us search in half the parameters.

experiments.hypothesis: The best shapes may need exact zeros and repeated equal heights that free-form height search reaches only by accident; a sparse sum of K boxes (3K parameters) can produce a flat-topped f*f directly and opens a different region of shape space.
experiments.change: Ignore start. Build f on an N=200 grid as f(x)=sum_{k=1..K} a_k * 1[l_k <= x < l_k+w_k], clipped to [0,1], with K in {3,4,5,6}, l_k in [0,1], w_k in [0,0.6], a_k in [0,3]. Stage 1: random search, 20000 samples drawn uniformly in those ranges (evaluate R on an N=100 grid for speed), keep the top 20. Stage 2: refine each of the top 20 with scipy.optimize.minimize(method='Powell', bounds=the ranges) on -R at N=100, 2000 max evaluations each. Stage 3: take the best parametrized f, evaluate it on the N=200 grid, then run coordinate ascent (step ladder 0.05,0.02,0.01,0.005,0.002*mean over all 200 heights) plus short perturbed restarts (perturb 5% of entries by 0.05*mean, 300 refine steps) until 95% of budget, keeping the global best. Print the best R after each stage and the winning K.
experiments.prediction: The box-sum family reaches 0.80-0.83; if it reaches >=0.83 it is a genuinely new structural line worth branching on.
experiments.if_gain: Next branch: take the winning K and box layout, allow per-box smooth edges (erf ramps) and unequal widths, re-optimize, and polish at N=400; compare its plateau fraction to p0012's.
experiments.if_not: If box-sums stay below ~0.81, conclude that many-level smooth profiles are essential and spend future explore slots on target-fitting (fit f so f*f approximates a trapezoid of varying plateau fraction) instead of sparse boxes.

A single-height change updates f*f exactly in O(N) (delta L[k] = 2*d*h_old[k-i] + d^2*[k==2i]), so exact R can be re-evaluated in O(N) — 100-1000x cheaper. That makes ~10^5 exact single-coordinate Metropolis trials at N=1600 affordable, a search regime never tried; coordinate moves alone failed before only because they were expensive and coarse.

Every 2000 trials run 40 exact-PGD steps (p0043's vectorised version) plus a softmax polish (tau 1e-3, 1e-4) on the current h, and resync L from h. Keep global best. Print acceptance rate, trial count and R every 5 s.

plan.analysis: p0048's incremental O(N) exact-R engine (+0.00070) and p0047's N=800 structured-move loop (+0.00055) both beat the old move+PGD loop on the same start, but they were never combined (F48). p0048's engine is still only single-coordinate: 528k trials, 32k accepted, yet gains came mostly from the periodic PGD/softmax polishes — so the move class, not the throughput, is now the limit. Bet 1: incremental *block* moves (delta L = 2*conv(d,h) + conv(d,d), still O(N·m)) give the cheap engine a structural move class it lacks. Bet 2: interleaving the coordinate engine with p0047's N=800 structured-move+softmax loop tests whether the two cheap engines are complementary or converge to one basin. Explore opens a dyadic greedy-refinement line: build f by recursively splitting blocks and choosing split ratios by exact R — a multi-scale construction never tried.

experiments.hypothesis: p0048's incremental engine only proposes single-coordinate changes, so it cannot make a coherent multi-cell deformation in one accepted step; block moves updated incrementally cost O(N*m) (m<=64) instead of a full convolve and should be accepted far more often, letting the search reshape whole shoulders of f*f rather than one pixel at a time.

In the main loop, with probability 0.5 do a BLOCK move instead: pick m log-uniform in {2,4,8,16,32,64}, start i uniform in [0,N-m], shape = constant, or linear ramp from d0 to 0, or 'flatten' (d = mean(h[i:i+m]) - h[i:i+m]); d0 = step*mean_h*exp(0.5*randn)*sign with the same geometric annealing of step from 0.3*mean to 1e-3*mean. Update L incrementally with c1 = np.convolve(dblk, h) added to L[i:i+m+N-1] (times 2) and c2 = np.convolve(dblk, dblk) added to L[2i:2i+2m-1]; recompute exact R via _R_from_L in O(N); on rejection subtract both. experiments.hypothesis: F48 asks whether the two cheap engines are complementary: p0048's coordinate Metropolis explores pixel-level rearrangements at N=1600 while p0047's N=800 structured moves + PGD + softmax polish explore coarse structural changes. Loop until 90% of budget: (a) 2.5 s of p0048's incremental single-coordinate Metropolis at N=1600 with its annealing and temperature; (b) downsample the current best by block-averaging to N=800 and run p0047's structured move loop for 3 s (8 move types incl. tilt, adaptive amplitude halving after 5 rejects / doubling after 3 accepts, 120-step exact PGD per move, accept only if exact R at N=800 improves, softmax polish tau 1e-3/1e-4 every 4 accepts); (c) upsample that result back to N=1600 by midpoint interpolation, run 80 exact-PGD steps + softmax polish (tau 1e-3, 1e-4), keep it only if its exact N=1600 R beats the best; once mid-run also try an N=3200 upsample probe with the same polish and keep if better. Final 4 s: pure N=1600 PGD + softmax polish on the best. Print the best R after each phase.
experiments.prediction: At least one phase (b)/(c) improves on the coordinate-only result; final exact R 0.8747-0.8760. If it lands within 1e-5 of 0.874544 the two engines share one basin.
experiments.if_gain: Next deepen reallocates the whole budget to the winning phase ratio (e.g., mostly N=800 moves with short N=1600 coordinate bursts) and adds N=3200 probes at every cycle.
experiments.if_not: If interleaving adds nothing, the two engines are redundant; next deepen abandons the N=800 loop and pushes the block-move engine at N=3200 with softmax polish instead.

experiments.hypothesis: The best shapes are multi-scale step functions (13% zeros, max/mean 6.5, plateau in f*f), but every existing line starts from a smooth bell or a K-box ansatz. A greedy dyadic construction — start flat, repeatedly split the block whose split most improves exact R, choosing the left/right height ratio from a small grid — builds a genuinely multi-scale staircase directly from the objective and can land in a basin no local search from a bell reaches.
experiments.change: From scratch (start=None). Build h at N=256, initially all ones. Maintain the set of dyadic blocks; repeatedly take the largest remaining unsplit block, and for that block try all 25 pairs (a,b) from multipliers {0.4,0.7,1.0,1.4,2.5} applied to the block's current height (left half = h*a, right half = h*b), evaluating exact R with a full np.convolve each time; keep the best pair and commit it. Continue until all blocks are of length 1 or ~40% of the budget is used. Then upsample to N=1024 by midpoint interpolation and spend the rest of the budget on exact PGD (backtracking, 100-step chunks) + softmax polish (tau 1e-3, 1e-4) alternated with p0048-style incremental single-coordinate Metropolis at N=1024, keeping the global best. Print R after the greedy phase and at each polish.
experiments.prediction: Greedy dyadic phase alone reaches R 0.78-0.83 at N=256; after upsampling and polish the fresh start lands at 0.84-0.87, opening a multi-scale line whose zero pattern and f*f peak position differ from the best line's (peak not at 0.772).
experiments.if_gain: Next branch takes the dyadic result, upsamples to N=1600 and runs the full coordinate-Metropolis + softmax polish engine, and tries a second greedy pass at N=1024 with finer ratio grids.
experiments.if_not: If it stalls below 0.84, greedy dyadic splits are too myopic; next explore keeps the multi-scale idea but optimizes all split ratios jointly with Powell on the log-ratios instead of greedily.

plan.analysis: p0053 (0.875495) won by adding random block moves (sizes 2-64, 5.3% accepted) on top of p0048's single-coordinate engine; the last increments still came from the periodic softmax polish, so the engine's job is to hand the polish a better-shaped basin. Two untested directions on that line: (a) random block directions are uninformed — a gradient-guided block step with an exact incremental line search should deform whole shoulders coherently and be accepted far more often; (b) the largest block is only 4% of N=1600 while the f*f plateau spans ~38% of knots, so genuinely coarse blocks (128-512) at small amplitude may be needed. For breadth I branch the box line p0050 (0.867803, N=200) — a different basin that has never seen the incremental block engine — upsampled and re-polished.

experiments.hypothesis: p0053's block moves pick random constant/ramp directions, so most are rejected (5.3%) and gains arrive only via the polish. A block move along the exact gradient restricted to a contiguous window is a coherent, informed multi-cell deformation; with an incremental exact line search over a few trial amplitudes it should be accepted at several times the random-block rate and reach shapes the polish alone cannot.
experiments.change: Start = p0053 heights (N=1600). Keep its stage A soft polish, its periodic exact-PGD + softmax polish cadence, its single-coordinate Metropolis, and its existing random block moves. Change the block half of the loop: with probability 0.5 do a GRADIENT block move instead. Cache g = _score_grad(h)[1] (exact gradient, vectorised) and recompute it after every accepted move and at least every 200 trials. Pick m log-uniform in {8,16,32,64,128}, i uniform in [0, N-m]; dblk = g[i:i+m]; scale so max|dblk| = step (same annealed step schedule as now); clip dblk so h[i:i+m]+dblk >= 0. Try amplitudes t = 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 2, 4 (in that order) applied to dblk, each evaluated by incrementally updating L (L[i:i+m+N-1] += 2*conv(dblk,h); L[2i:2i+2m-1] += conv(dblk,dblk)) and computing exact R via _R_from_L; accept the first t that improves R (else Metropolis-accept the t=1 candidate and revert L otherwise). Track and print acceptance separately for gradient-block, random-block and single moves.
experiments.prediction: Gradient-block acceptance 15-35% vs 5.3% for random blocks, and final exact R >= 0.8758 (above 0.875495), with the 0.1%-of-max knot share above 31%.
experiments.if_gain: Next deepen drops random blocks entirely, uses gradient blocks at all scales including 256, and re-tunes the polish cadence (more frequent, tighter tau) since the engine will then be feeding it better candidates.
experiments.if_not: If gradient blocks are accepted often but R does not move, the block direction is not the limit and the next deepen switches to coarse random blocks (128-512) and to the polish schedule; if they are rarely accepted, the cached gradient is stale and the next deepen recomputes it every trial on a smaller N=800 grid.

experiments.hypothesis: p0053's block sizes stop at 64 (4% of N=1600) while the f*f plateau spans ~38% of knots and the shape has 13.6% zeros and max/mean 6.28: reshaping the broad shoulders needs deformations over 128-512 cells. Coarse blocks at small amplitude (mass-matched to a fine block) are a different, gentler move than p0052's multiplicative segment-scale, which collapsed because it rescaled whole segments by large factors.
experiments.change: Start = p0053 heights (N=1600). Keep everything (stage A soft polish, single-coordinate moves, sizes 2-64 blocks, periodic polish) and extend the block move: with probability 0.5 of block trials choose m from {128, 256, 512} (else from {2,4,8,16,32,64} as now). For coarse m use only two shapes: (a) constant d0, (b) linear ramp from d0 to 0, with d0 = 0.1 * step * sqrt(64/m) * exp(0.5*randn) * sign (i.e. amplitude shrunk so total mass change matches a fine block); never use the full 'flatten' shape for m>64. Clip to non-negativity, update L incrementally exactly as now (2*conv(dblk,h) and conv(dblk,dblk)), same Metropolis temperature and global best. Print acceptance rate and number of accepted moves separately for size classes <=64 and >64.
experiments.prediction: Coarse (m>64) acceptance at least 1.5-2%, with at least a few accepted coarse moves that raise best R; final exact R 0.8756-0.8762. If coarse acceptance is below 0.5% and no coarse move ever enters the best, the basin is rigid above scale 64.
experiments.if_gain: Next deepen makes coarse blocks the dominant move class, adds a coarse-block version of the gradient line search, and probes N=3200 with block sizes doubled.
experiments.if_not: Conclude the basin is rigid above ~64 cells at N=1600 and spend the next deepen on the polish schedule (frequent tight-tau softmax PGD, tau down to 1e-5) and on the gradient-block direction instead.

experiments.hypothesis: The box line (p0050, 0.867803 at N=200) is a genuinely different basin from the free-height line but has only ever been polished by PGD/Powell-style moves. Upsampling it to N=1600 and giving it p0053's incremental single-coordinate + block Metropolis engine plus periodic softmax polish tests whether the box basin reaches the same plateau or a better one.
experiments.change: Start = p0050 heights (N=200). Upsample to N=1600 by linear interpolation (np.interp on cell centres) as the working array, keeping the original N=200 array as a fallback best. Then run p0053's pipeline verbatim on the N=1600 array: stage A soft polish (tau 1e-3 then 1e-4, 60 PGD steps each), then the Metropolis loop with single-coordinate moves (10% zeroing) and block moves of sizes {2,4,8,16,32,64} (constant/ramp/flatten), incremental L updates, the same annealed step (0.3*mean -> 1e-3*mean) and temperature, and periodic exact-PGD + softmax polish every ~4 s. Keep the global best across both resolutions; report both the N=200 and N=1600 best R.
experiments.prediction: The upsampled box start polishes to at least 0.870 and the engine lifts it to 0.872-0.876; if it exceeds 0.8755 the box basin is competitive with the free-height line and deserves its own deepens.
experiments.if_gain: Next branch returns to the N=200 box parametrisation (K boxes) and re-fits the box parameters with the engine's best shape as target, then re-expands — a two-resolution loop.

Add ONE new move class, used in 25% of block trials: pick m uniformly from {128,256,512} and a random start i; compute g = _score_grad(h)[1], take w = g[i:i+m] and normalize w /= max|w|; set d = zeros(N), d[i:i+m] = w; run an exact incremental line search over amplitudes alpha = step * 2^k for k in -6..+2 and both signs (step = 0.3*mean_h*(1e-3/0.3)**(1-frac) as now), computing delta L = 2*np.convolve(alpha*d, h)[:2N-1] + np.convolve(alpha*d, alpha*d)[:2N-1], new_R = _R_from_L(L+deltaL, s+alpha*d.sum()), and accept the best alpha greedily if it beats cur_R. experiments.hypothesis: R is exactly the flatness of f*f: a perfect box would give R=1, and the current best is 0.8758 with 34% of knots within 0.1% of max. No line has ever optimised a shape target directly. Alternating projection of f*f onto a box target (gradient descent on ||f*f - T||^2 with non-negativity and mass renormalisation) is a genuinely different construction that should produce very flat autoconvolutions.
experiments.change: From scratch, no start. N=512, domain [0,1]. For each target width Wk in {0.35,0.5,0.65,0.8}*(2N-1): T = H*indicator over the centred window of length Wk, with H = (sum h)^2 / Wk. Init h = cosine bump (0.5*(1-cos(2*pi*x)) with x=(arange(N)+0.5)/N). Iterate 400 steps: L = np.convolve(h,h); r = L - T; grad = 2*np.convolve(r, h[::-1])[N-1:2N-1]; h = np.maximum(h - lr*grad, 0) with lr = 1e-3*(h.mean())/(max|grad|+1e-12); rescale h so sum(h)=1. Record exact R for each Wk. Take the best h, upsample to N=1600 by np.interp, run 200 exact-PGD steps then a 6 s incremental single-coordinate + block Metropolis chain with one polish at the end. Print R after projection and after polish for every Wk.
experiments.prediction: Projection reaches raw R 0.80-0.86; after polish 0.86-0.87, below 0.8758 but high enough to show the flat-target family is viable.
experiments.if_gain: If it reaches >=0.87, next branch sweeps Wk finely and adds a two-parameter trapezoid target (plateau width plus ramp width) and runs the full engine.
experiments.if_not: The flat-target projection family is inferior; next explore tries f = sum of K shifted copies of a base step shape with weights optimised by a short local search on R.

plan.analysis: The best line has plateaued: the last four gains were +2e-5, +3e-5, +3e-5, +0. Every gain on this line has come from the periodic polish, yet that polish is still crude steepest ascent with backtracking, run only 80 steps at a time, and never uses curvature even though the exact gradient is already coded. Meanwhile every structured construction (box target, dyadic, cascade) stalls at ~0.80, so the free-form basin is the only productive region. Bet: the polish is the remaining lever, and a genuine second-order method (L-BFGS-B with the exact/softmax gradient, renormalised between rounds) converges much deeper than 80 PGD steps. I test it twice, inside the best engine (deepen) and on the second-best distinct basin, the box line p0059 at 0.8689 (branch), to separate 'basin-limited' from 'polish-limited'. Explore opens a random multi-start + L-BFGS line to test whether the 0.8758 basin is special.

experiments.hypothesis: All recent gains on this line came from the periodic polish, but that polish is steepest ascent with backtracking (80 steps, no curvature) while the exact analytic gradient is already available. A second-order polish (L-BFGS-B, bounds h>=0) on the softmax-smoothed R at annealed tau should converge far deeper in the same time, so the plateau is polish-limited rather than exhausted.
experiments.change: Start = p0072 heights (N=1600). Delete the gradient-guided coarse block move class (F67: 0.2% acceptance, zero gain) and the 80-step stage-A PGD. Add helper `_lbfgs_polish(h)`: for tau in (1e-3, 1e-4, 1e-5) call scipy.optimize.minimize(lambda z: (-R, -grad) from the existing `_score_grad_soft(z, tau)` with jac=True, method='L-BFGS-B', bounds=[(0.0, None)]*N, options={'maxiter':500,'ftol':1e-16,'gtol':1e-14,'maxls':40}); after each tau renormalise h to mean 1 (R is scale-invariant) and keep the best-by-exact-R array; finish with 30 exact-max PGD steps. Call `_lbfgs_polish` from best_h at 0.12, 0.30, 0.50, 0.70 and 0.88 of the budget, restarting the Metropolis chain from the polished point each time. Keep the existing incremental single-coordinate + block Metropolis between polishes unchanged.
experiments.prediction: If polish-limited, final R rises by at least +3e-5 (>= 0.87581) and the 0.1%-of-max knot share rises above 34%, with L-BFGS hitting gradient norm < 1e-6 before maxiter. If the basin is converged, every L-BFGS call returns within 1e-5 of its start and final R stays at 0.875776 +/- 1e-5.
experiments.if_gain: Make L-BFGS the only polish (drop PGD entirely), raise maxiter, extend the tau ladder to 1e-6, and add basin hopping: after each convergence perturb the 20 cells with largest gradient by 1% and re-polish, keeping the exact-R best.
experiments.if_not: The N=1600 basin is a genuine local optimum with no curvature headroom; next deepen abandons local polish and spends the whole budget on structured basin escapes (coherent reshuffles of the plateau shoulders) and re-tests N=3200 with the L-BFGS polish.

experiments.hypothesis: The box line (p0059, 0.868859 at N=1600) is the best non-best basin: its f*f peaks at 0.375 with only 20.9% of knots within 0.1% of max, versus 0.689 and 33.8% for the best, and it has only ever been polished by steepest-ascent PGD. If its 0.007 deficit is polish-limited rather than basin-limited, the L-BFGS polish should move it by >= 0.003; if it moves by < 0.001 the box basin is genuinely worse.
experiments.change: Start = p0059 heights (N=1600). Spend the first 45% of the budget on repeated `_lbfgs_polish` (same helper as the deepen: tau ladder 1e-3/1e-4/1e-5, L-BFGS-B with h>=0 bounds, mean-1 renormalisation, exact-R best kept) run from the start and from 3 perturbed copies (multiply a random 20%-wide window by 0.8 or 1.25, renormalise). Then run p0066's incremental single-coordinate + block Metropolis with polish-from-best at 0.15 cadence for the remaining budget, keeping the global best by exact R. Report exact R at N=1600 and, if time allows, at the upsampled N=3200.

experiments.if_not: Distinct basins are not reachable by these structural moves; next deepen reverts to single-incumbent hopping but at N=3200 with mass-conserving resampling, testing whether the limit is resolution rather than basin structure.
